questions.question: The sum of the length and breadth of a cuboid is 40 cm. If the height of the cuboid is 1/5 of the sum of its length and breadth, then what is the lateral surface area of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Lateral Surface Area (LSA)** of a **cuboid** = **Perimeter of base** × **Height**

Perimeter of base = 2 × (l + b) = 2 × 40 = 80 cm.

**Height (h)** = 1/5 × (l + b) = 1/5 × 40 = 8 cm.

LSA = 80 × 8 = 640 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 640 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of **length (l)** and **breadth (b)** = 40 cm

**Height (h)** = (1/5) × (l + b)

**Formula Used:**

**Lateral Surface Area (LSA)** = 2h(l + b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f669cf197fb8066be38c886f1af7db7f01d9417d5b21317bf48721228546927.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ l + b = 40 cm

⇒ h = (1/5) × 40 = 8 cm

⇒ LSA = 2 × (l + b) × h

⇒ LSA = 2 × 40 × 8

⇒ LSA = 80 × 8

⇒ LSA = 640 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 640 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cuboid

The total area of all six faces is given by the formula: **TSA** = 2(lb + bh + hl).

Volume of Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as: **Volume** = length × breadth × height (l × b × h).

Diagonal of Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid has length: **Diagonal** = √(l² + b² + h²).</p

+ and ÷

I. 9 ÷ 6 × 4 + 2 - 5 = 16

II. 5 - 28 + 7 × 16 ÷ 4= -103
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png]

⇒ 9 + __**6 × 2**__ - 5 = 16

⇒ __**9 + 12**__ - 5 = 16

⇒ __**21 - 5**__ = 16

⇒ 16 = 16

⇒ 5 - __**28 ÷ 7**__ × 16 + 4 = -103

⇒ 5 - __**4 × 16**__ + 4 = -103

⇒ __**5**__ - 64 __**+ 4**__ = -103

⇒ __**9**____** - 64**__ = -103

⇒ **-55 ≠ -103**

**LHS ≠ RHS**

∴ Here, Conclusion II is not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only II".**

• The BPL benchmark is used by the government **to target various social welfare programs and schemes to the poorest and most vulnerable sections of society.**

• **It is a pricing strategy that involves setting different prices for products within a product line, based on their perceived value or quality. **
 
• The goal of base price lining is to maximize profits by offering customers a range of choices at different price points, while still maintaining a consistent brand image.
 
 
 
• **Below Price Line:-**
 
 
• **It is a term used to describe products that are priced below the average market price for similar products.**
 
• This can be done for a variety of reasons, such as to attract new customers, to increase sales volume, or to clear out inventory.

questions.question: Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of ______.

• **Sati:-**

 
 
• It is the name of an ancient Indian practice where women would die in the pyre of her dead husband.
 
• The practice was voluntary but most of the time, it was involuntary.
 
• If a woman had no surviving children who could support her, she was pressured to accept sati.
 
• Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of Sati.
 
• Bentinck passed the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829.
 
 
• He issued Regulation XVII declaring Sati to be illegal and punishable in criminal courts.
 
• The ban was met by uproar because many people supported Sati at the time.
 
• The matter went to the Privy Council in London.
